$comment: P69 L2a (lane lm, D-C-SIZEOF-OF-A-VLA-TYPED-OPERAND-SKIPS-THE-OPERANDS-SIDE-EFFECTS): what C evaluates in a variable-length operand or a variably modified type name is evaluated, once, and nothing else is. A sizeof whose operand has variable-length array type evaluates it (C 6.5.3.4p2) - an index with a side effect, a call (counted: once), an assignment, two indices, a fixed-outer array's row, a pointer stepped on the way, a typeof of a row in a type name, every iteration of a loop - and answers the size the operand's root froze; a cast's and a compound literal's variably modified type name runs its size expressions (C 6.7.6.2p5, C23 6.7.2.5p4). A fixed type, a variable-length array's fixed row or element, a comma that decays, a nested sizeof, every alignof spelling and a sizeof of a pointer type are NOT evaluated. MEASURED at 937a3b15 (the orchestrator's compile-and-keep, macos-arm64-debug, x86_64:pe64, images run natively, baseline and release alike): every evaluated form left its side effect undone (sizeof v[k++] left k == 0; the program's probes ran 1 where the references run 41). gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 build THIS file at -std=gnu2x and -std=c2x -pedantic-errors and exit 42 (clang warns -Wunevaluated-expression on the unevaluated checks, which is their point). Exit 42, or the number of the first check that fails. The release arm runs the same evaluations through the optimizer.
